labeller: labeller 2: claude-opus-5-5 through `claude -p` with every tool switched off (`--tools ""`), no MCP server (`--strict-mcp-config` with an empty config), no settings sources and no session persistence, run from an empty directory; given only labeller-2-prompt.txt (seed 21082): policy-v1 and the 25 requirements in a seeded order. It saw no label, no rule summary, no code, no prompt of the product and no arm. It is not the agent that chose the requirements.

applies.reason: It asks for the new-password field to be masked, the same as the other password fields.
The admin reset flow has the admin type the user's new password, so the admin knows it.
A separate SAML2 IdP is proposed, with no statement on verifying authentication strength from the IdP response.
applies.businessFact: Does OpenEMR need a specific authentication strength or method (e.g. MFA) from the IdP for any functions?

applies.reason: Session lifetime and re-authentication between OpenEMR and the IdP are not defined.
applies.businessFact: What is the maximum time allowed between IdP authentication events before OpenEMR must require re-authentication?

applies.reason: Workstation-login SSO may be single-factor, and it does not say whether the IdP enforces MFA.
applies.businessFact: Will the SSO identity provider enforce multi-factor authentication for OpenEMR users?

applies.reason: The generated portal password is fixed to be returned, with no statement that it expires or cannot become the long-term password.
applies.businessFact: Must the system-generated portal password expire after first use or a short period, forcing the patient to set their own?

applies.reason: In the admin reset flow the admin sets the user's new password.
It changes lockout-counter behaviour, and it does not say whether the security documentation calls for clearing the counter on admin reset.
applies.businessFact: Does the security documentation require the failed-login counter to be cleared when an administrator resets a user's password?

applies.reason: It explicitly removes all character-composition requirements.
The password policy is changed without stating the minimum length that remains.
applies.businessFact: What minimum password length (at least 8, ideally 15) will the policy keep once composition rules are removed?

applies.reason: A show/hide toggle is the permitted temporary view of a masked password field.
It builds notifications around password expiry, which keeps periodic credential rotation in place.
It asks for 'detailed' password administration logging without stating what metadata each entry holds.
applies.businessFact: Which fields (timestamp, acting admin, target user, source IP, action) must each password administration log entry record?

applies.reason: Logout ends in an error, and it does not say whether the server-side session is invalidated.
applies.businessFact: Is the patient's portal session invalidated on the server when logout is triggered, before the redirect fails?

applies.reason: On token expiry the user must be logged out automatically and sent to the login screen.
A CSRF token is carried in the URL query string, and no remediation moving it to the body or headers is specified.
The upgrade scripts that change ACLs and schema run with authentication skipped, and no access restriction is specified.
It trusts X-Forwarded-For only from trusted proxies and stores remote and forwarded IPs as separate structured fields, so the 'where' metadata is accurate.
Client-supplied header text is persisted, and it does not say whether forwarded_for is validated or encoded before logging.
applies.businessFact: Will the forwarded_for value be validated as IP addresses or encoded before it is written to the audit log?

applies.reason: TOTP is added, but whether it is required depends on a portal_force_mfa toggle.
applies.businessFact: Will portal_force_mfa be enabled so that every patient must use a second factor to access the portal?

applies.reason: It says nothing on whether the portal forgotten-password reset will bypass the newly enrolled MFA.
applies.businessFact: Must the portal password reset flow require the patient's enrolled second factor before access is granted?

applies.reason: INSERT/SELECT-only grants and checksum chaining prevent modification, but removing the default DB user's read access is only 'ideally', and encryption is being removed.
applies.businessFact: Will the default openemr database user be denied all access to the log tables, leaving only a dedicated least-privilege account?

applies.reason: Edit capability is granted on the basis of the explicitly assigned Demographics Write permission.
New admin unblock surfaces are added without stating which permission restricts them.
applies.businessFact: Which ACL permission is required to view and clear the MFA and portal-account lockout counters?

applies.reason: Manual clearing of brute-force counters changes the throttling control, and it does not say whether the security documentation allows this.
applies.businessFact: Does the security documentation permit administrators to manually clear brute-force lockout counters before the window expires?
